subject: religion
title: Islamic Ethics and Society
summary: Social responsibilities, family values, neighbourhood rights, and environmental ethics in Islam

sections.title: Social Responsibilities in Islam
sections.content: Islam emphasizes the importance of social responsibility. Every Muslim has duties toward others in society. These include caring for the poor and needy through Zakat (obligatory charity) and Sadaqah (voluntary charity). Islam commands justice, honesty, and fairness in all dealings. The concept of Amr bil Ma'ruf wa Nahi anil Munkar (enjoining good and forbidding evil) encourages Muslims to promote virtue and prevent harm. Students learn that helping others is an act of worship.

sections.title: Family Values and Relationships
sections.content: The family is the foundation of Islamic society. Respect and kindness toward parents are emphasised throughout the Quran: 'And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy' (Surah Al-Isra, 17:24). Parents deserve care especially in old age. Spouses should live with love, mercy, and mutual respect. Children have the right to love, education, and proper upbringing. Maintaining family ties (silatur rahim) is a religious duty, and cutting family relations is considered a major sin.

sections.title: Neighbourhood Rights and Community Life
sections.content: Islam grants extensive rights to neighbours. The Prophet Muhammad (SM) said: 'Jibril kept advising me about the neighbour until I thought he would make him an heir.' Neighbours, regardless of religion, deserve respect, help, and consideration. Muslims should share food with neighbours, avoid causing harm, and visit the sick. Community life includes attending mosque prayers, participating in funerals, and supporting community welfare. Good citizenship means obeying laws and contributing positively to society.

sections.title: Environmental Ethics in Islam
sections.content: Islam teaches that humans are stewards (khalifah) of the Earth, responsible for its care. The Quran describes nature as a sign of Allah's creation. Wastefulness (israf) is prohibited: 'Eat and drink, but waste not by excess' (Surah Al-A'raf, 7:31). Planting trees, conserving water, and protecting animals are acts of charity. Students learn Islamic guidelines for environmental conservation: avoiding pollution, preserving natural resources, and maintaining cleanliness in public spaces.
